alt: The guiding principle of Human ingenuity, explore the ways in which human creativity and innovation affect our world, sits above a central circle joined to five optional recommended topics: entertainment, artistic expressions, communication and media, technology and scientific innovation. Two possible questions sit below as lenses.
caption: Five optional topics and two possible questions: a starting map, not a fence.

after: ## How the theme reaches the assessment
alt: A bar splits the course into four equal 25 percent parts: Paper 1 writing (30 marks), Paper 2 listening (25 marks), Paper 2 reading (40 marks) and the internally assessed individual oral (30 marks). Cards note that Human ingenuity can appear in any of them.
caption: Human ingenuity can feed Paper 1, both halves of Paper 2 and the oral.

alt: Three linked cards: the idea, how it was made, and what it changes, the last highlighted. A table shows that a text about a new vaccine also touches Identities and one about solar power touches Sharing the planet, but under Human ingenuity the questions are about the creation and its effects.
caption: The guiding principle is about effect: always reach what the creation changes.

after: ## Worked example 1: learning about a culture from its art
alt: Four numbered steps: describe the jars and the blue fish precisely; infer that the community values continuity with room for individual creativity; answer the question with the quotation it is just a jar; then learn target-language frames for interpretation. Steps 2 and 3 are highlighted as where the marks sit.
caption: Description is only step 1: the marks are in inferring and answering.

after: ## Worked example 2: how media change relationships
alt: Four linked cards for one argument: point (messaging keeps families in daily contact across countries), example (a grandmother watches a school play on a video call), effect (closeness despite distance) and counterpoint (a screen is not a visit, and not every grandparent has a device). The model paragraph concludes that the media have changed what closeness means.
caption: Point, example, effect, counterpoint: one counterpoint makes the argument credible.

after: ## Paper 1: planning a response on this theme
alt: Chips set the context (school magazine), audience (other students), purpose (inform and persuade) and register (lively, semi-formal). Five linked boxes give the review's shape: title, an opening that puts the reader in the headset, what works, what is lost, and a clear recommendation.
caption: A review weighs what works against what is lost, then gives a verdict.

alt: Four linked cards for the SL oral: describe (who, what, where), interpret (why it was made), connect (to the theme and a target-language culture) and judge (your view with a reason). Example images include a mural and a robot in a hospital. At HL the stimulus is a literary excerpt.
caption: Describe, interpret, connect, judge: always reach an opinion.
